newsitem.title: UK: UK oil stocks higher after strong U.S. showing.
newsitem.headline: UK oil stocks higher after strong U.S. showing.

text.p: Shares in major UK listed oil companies were firmer on Wednesday against a weaker overall market trend, following a robust performance by energy stocks in the U.S. on Tuesday, market makers said.
A firmer crude price also helped market sentiment, they said.
"The oils have been strong for sometime. People think there is still a lot of value in the sector," one market maker said.
British Petroleum Plc was up 5p to 692-1/2 after its ADRs in the U.S. added $2-1/8 to $134-1/4, Enterprise rose 3p to 614p and Shell Transport and Trading Plc rose 2-1/2p to 10.59 stg by 0830 GMT.
On Wall Street on Tuesday, oil stocks were the star performers in an otherwise weak Dow Industrials average. Texaco rose $3-1/2 to $101-7/8 while Exxon Corp gained $7/8 to $100.
Dealers said the sector was also helped by the stronger price of crude oil, which has been in a two-month downtrend.

April Brent crude futures, which rose 58 cents to $19.50 a barrel in London on Tuesday, were quoted on SIMEX in Singapore at $19.65/$19.75 on Wednesday, pushed higher by the latest weekly U.S. crude stock inventory report.

The American Petroleum Institute stock data, released late in New York on Tuesday, showed an unexpected fall in crude oil stocks of 7.6 million barrels. A build of 2.8 million barrels had been expected.
